PackFileChange.description: One file that differs between two pins of a pack: the manifest, a hook, a script.

lines.description: The changed lines of a text file: `@@`, `-` and `+` lines, no context.

note.description: Why there are no lines, when there are none to show.

PackFileChangeKind.description: How a file of the pack differs between two pins.

oneOf.description: A file that became a folder, a link or a submodule, or the other way round.

PackReviewData.description:
What a person is shown before trusting a pack (0.9, Per pack source): where it is from, the hooks, providers and
observers it runs, and what it requires.

commit.description: The commit a `git:` source resolved to. Absent for a `dev:` folder.

observers.description: A key holds the events the observer gets.

tree.description: The tree id the pack is trusted at.

PackReviewLine.description: One script or provider a pack runs, with the manifest key that names it.

TrustChange.description:
One thing the trust hash covers that is new, gone or different since the person trusted the line: `board.yaml`, a
pack's folder, a view. A folder shows its changed `files`; a file shows its changed `lines`. Where neither can be
shown, `note` says why.

TrustChangeKind.description: How one thing the trust hash covers differs from what was trusted.

TrustPackReview.description: A pack of the line that its repo supplies, with what it runs.

TrustState.description:
Whether a line's packs and gate code are trusted (0.9, Trust). `hash` is what trust covers now: the packs, the
lock, the pointer file, `board.yaml`, `config.yaml`, the views and the tree hashes of `protectedPaths`. It is the
hash an `Untrusted` line would be trusted at, so the person is shown what they trust. (The domain record is plain
Rust, so the wire form is this type.)

oneOf.description: Nothing is trusted yet, or the hash changed since.

description:
`board.trust_review` result: what a person sees before they trust a line. `hash` is the one `board.trust` takes. It
is empty when the line did not load: `problems` says why, `hosts` holds the hosts a fetch would contact for the
first time and `dev_folders` the `dev:` folders never trusted, and approving them (a `board.trust` with an empty
hash) lets the load go on. `changes` are against what was trusted, or everything as added when nothing was.
title: BoardTrustReviewResult
